failed.name: Chakdara
failed.why: a mountain tributary. GloFAS at 5 km does not resolve this channel: measured against eight mountain gauges the day-to-day change in modelled discharge correlates with the observed change at 0.00. Held in the list so the refusal is explicit rather than the point simply being absent.

tarbela.method: Gumbel (EV1) by the method of moments on annual maxima of the GloFAS reanalysis, 1997-01-01 onward
tarbela.caveat: fitted to the MODEL reanalysis, not to gauge records. A "10-year" level here is a discharge this model exceeds about once a decade in its own record; it is a scale for change, not a calibrated flood frequency.
tarbela.abstractionCaveat: the reanalysis carries NO canal withdrawal. This build’s own fitted levels say so plainly: Guddu 16176, Sukkur 15928 and Kotri 16227 m3/s agree within 2 % across two of the largest irrigation barrages on earth, and Attock matches Tarbela and Chashma matches Taunsa the same way. On the lower Indus these levels describe a river with its diversions left in, which is not the river that reaches the barrage.
tarbela.sampleCaveat: fitted on 30 annual maxima. That supports the 2, 5 and 10-year levels; the 20 and 50-year levels are extrapolations beyond the record and should be read as order-of-magnitude, not as design values.

sidhnai.why: a Gumbel fit is REFUSED for this reach: the annual maxima have a coefficient of variation of 1.83, and Gumbel has a fixed skewness of 1.14 — a sample this dispersed is not the shape this distribution describes; the fitted 50-year level (446.1) is only 55 % of the observed 30-year maximum (808.1), which is far outside what sampling alone explains. No return levels are published for it.
